input.question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?
input.ground_truth: Because you remember the best, eventful memories in more detail. You tend to block out all the normal things like changing you socks or taking a shit that day. Similar to when you zone out in the shower trying to think if you've just washed your hair or not. You do those things everyday and block them out of memory.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy that you really loved when you were little. Now, when you look at a picture of you playing with that toy, you remember how much fun you had, and it feels super happy and perfect. But if you actually played with that toy again now, maybe the batteries are dead or it’s a little broken, and it’s not as fun as you remember.

When we remember things from the past, our brain likes to show us the happy and good parts, and sometimes forgets the not-so-good parts. So, things from the past seem even better in our memories than they really were. It’s like looking at a drawing you made and only remembering how cool it looked, not the mistakes you made with the crayon.
